# Kyoto Spring Trip Plan for 2 Adults

A 4-day Kyoto plan built around temples, food markets, moderate walking, and one gentler day for knee comfort. Budget target is kept near **$1,200 total excluding international flights**, with local transport and meals estimated in USD.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

### Day 1: Higashiyama Welcome Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Kiyomizu-dera, then a relaxed stroll down Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka.
- **Afternoon:** Kodai-ji area, Yasaka Shrine, and a tea break in Gion.
- **Food:** Lunch at a casual udon/soba shop; dinner near Gion or Pontocho.
- **Local transport:** **$12–$18**
- **Meal budget:** **$70–$95**
- **Rainy-day backup:** Kyoto National Museum + Nishiki Market covered-food stop + café time.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Rainy-day backup:** Kyoto National Museum + Nishiki Market covered-food stop + café time, Kyoto, Japan

### Day 2: Arashiyama and Western Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Arashiyama Bamboo Grove early, then Tenryu-ji.
- **Afternoon:** Togetsukyo Bridge, riverside break, and optional Okochi Sanso if energy is good.
- **Food:** Bento or tofu lunch in Arashiyama; simple izakaya-style dinner back in central Kyoto.
- **Local transport:** **$14–$22**
- **Meal budget:** **$75–$100**
- **Rainy-day backup:** Railway Museum or Kyoto Aquarium, then Arashiyama shops and cafés.

### Day 3: Slower Pace Day for Knee Comfort
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- **Morning:** Nishiki Market at an easy pace, with seated snack breaks.
- **Afternoon:** Kyoto Imperial Palace Park or Kyoto Gyoen for flat, low-strain walking.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ee/Shugaku-in_Imperial_Villa_-_Lower_Garden_a.JPG Alt=Afternoon:** Kyoto Imperial Palace Park or Kyoto Gyoen for flat, low-strain walking, Kyoto, Japan
- **Food:** Market grazing for lunch; kaiseki-lite or set meal dinner in central Kyoto.
- **Local transport:** **$10–$16**
- **Meal budget:** **$85–$120**
- **Rainy-day backup:** Nishiki Market, Daimaru depachika food floor, and a long café or tea-house stop.

### Day 4: Fushimi Inari and Sake District
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- **Morning:** Fushimi Inari Taisha; keep it to the lower shrine area or a partial climb to protect the knee.
- **Afternoon:** Fushimi sake district for tastings, canal-side strolls, and a relaxed late lunch.
- **Food:** Sake-friendly lunch set, then an easy final dinner in Kyoto Station area.
- **Local transport:** **$12–$20**
- **Meal budget:** **$70–$105**
- **Rainy-day backup:** Fushimi sake museums, Kyoto Station shopping, and a covered food court meal.

## Budget and Pace Comparison

| Day | Main Focus | Transport Cost | Meal Budget | Walking Load | Rainy-Day Fit |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Day 1 | Higashiyama temples + Gion | $12–$18 | $70–$95 | Moderate | Very good |
| Day 2 | Arashiyama nature + temples | $14–$22 | $75–$100 | Moderate | Good |
| Day 3 | Markets + flat park time | $10–$16 | $85–$120 | Light | Excellent |
Media: Alt=| Day 3 | Markets + flat park time | $10–$16 | $85–$120 | Light | Excellent |, Kyoto, Japan
| Day 4 | Fushimi Inari + sake area | $12–$20 | $70–$105 | Moderate, adjustable | Good |

## Budget Fit for 2 Adults

- **Estimated local transport total:** **$48–$76**
- **Estimated meals total:** **$300–$420**
- **Estimated sightseeing/admissions total:** **$80–$180**
- **Estimated lodging allowance from remaining budget:** **about $520–$772**
- **Total trip spend target:** **within $1,200**, assuming midrange budget lodging and modest entry fees
